**Narrative**

The enrichment analysis points decisively to **Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG map00260)** as the dominant affected pathway (FDR = 0.0, fold-enrichment = 603.3). Seven of the eleven input metabolites map to this pathway: choline, phosphoserine, sarcosine, AMP, S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), lipoic acid, and L-cystathionine. A tightly overlapping set of SMPDB disease entries — 3-phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase deficiency, dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase deficiency, and dimethylglycine dehydrogenase deficiency — all share the same metabolite cluster and reinforce a broader perturbation of one-carbon and amino-acid metabolism.

**Key drivers.** SAM (C00019) sits at the methyl-donation hub of this network. L-Cystathionine (C02291) is a direct downstream product of SAM via the trans-sulfuration pathway (SAM → S-adenosylhomocysteine → homocysteine → cystathionine), a relationship confirmed by KEGG BFS (path length = 3 hops). Choline (C00114) is an upstream precursor of methionine and therefore of SAM (path length = 4 hops). Phosphoserine (C01005) feeds into the serine–glycine axis that intersects with one-carbon folates, while sarcosine (C00213) is a glycine-derivative intermediate. Lipoic acid (C16241) — a required cofactor for mitochondrial dehydrogenase complexes — further anchors the phenotype to mitochondrial energy metabolism. UMP (C00105) and AMP (C00020) indicate broader nucleotide and energy-charge disturbances.

**Biological significance.** Coordinated changes in SAM, cystathionine, choline, and lipoic acid are characteristic of disrupted **one-carbon metabolism**, which governs methylation reactions, glutathione synthesis, and redox homeostasis. When SAM-dependent methylation fluxes shift, downstream trans-sulfuration intermediates such as cystathionine accumulate or deplete, directly impacting homocysteine detoxification. The presence of lipoic acid dysregulation suggests impairment of mitochondrial oxidative metabolism, while altered nucleotide monophosphates point to disturbed energy status. Together, these metabolites describe a metabolic state consistent with oxidative stress, altered methyl-group flux, and compromised mitochondrial function — a pattern reported in conditions ranging from fatty liver disease to neurodegeneration.
